title:
TRIGONOMETRY,
(SINE AND COSINE RULES)
objective: LO: I can apply the sine rule and cosine rule to find unknown sides and angles in non-right-angled triangles.

content.text: The sine rule is used when you have a side and its opposite angle: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C. The cosine rule is used when you know two sides and the included angle (or all three sides).
Cosine rule: a² = b² + c² - 2bc cos A. To find an angle: cos A = (b² + c² - a²) ÷ 2bc.

key_idea.title: Key idea
key_idea.text: Sine rule for matched pairs (side + opposite angle). Cosine rule for SAS or SSS.
key_idea.caption: Each side is proportional to the sine of its opposite angle

modelled_examples.label: Example 1 – sine rule finding a side
modelled_examples.question: In triangle ABC, A = 40°, B = 70°, a = 8. Find b.
modelled_examples.explanation: Cross-multiply to find the unknown side.

modelled_examples.label: Example 2 – sine rule finding an angle
modelled_examples.question: In triangle, a = 10, b = 7, A = 50°. Find B.
steps: sin B / b = sin A / a
modelled_examples.explanation: Use the sine rule flipped to find the angle.

modelled_examples.label: Example 3 – cosine rule finding a side
modelled_examples.question: b = 5, c = 7, A = 60°. Find a.
modelled_examples.explanation: Substitute into the cosine rule formula.

modelled_examples.label: Example 4 – cosine rule finding an angle
modelled_examples.question: a = 8, b = 6, c = 5. Find angle A.
modelled_examples.explanation: A negative value of cos means the angle is obtuse.
